by_hand.note: Counts only a person can supply. Each is changed here, by hand, when the other party agrees to be counted; python scripts/bench_docs.py then writes it into the table of docs/NUMBERS.md.

facts.what: repositories in the index with an agent pull request that claims tests or CI pass
of those, the ones whose first such pull request had a failed check of any kind at its head commit (any_check_failed)
of the 826, the ones where a failed check was, by its name, a test, build, lint or type-check job (test_or_build_check_failed)
THE LEAD NUMBER: of the 241, the ones with a failed test, build, lint or type-check job at the head commit, after the second reading of docs/index_review.json (method version 1, docs/INDEX_METHOD.md)
cheating pull requests in the tamper benchmark (21 ideas in each of three sample repositories), and how many passed plain CI
the minimum fee, in a token with 6 decimals such as USDC
the release fee decided 23 Oct 2026, paid by the company on top; not on chain until the timelocked upgrade
the solver keeps 100% of what they are paid; the company pays the payment costs on top of the 1% release fee
cards cover milestones up to 500 USD; a larger milestone is paid in by bank transfer or USDC
demand checks a month that are free, decided 23 Oct 2026

days of public delay before an upgrade of the second deployment can execute: the time lock (691,200 seconds, in force since 11 Oct 2026) of the Squads multisig `upgrade_multisig` in programs-v2/program_ids.json, whose vault is the programs' upgrade authority
both programs of the first deployment are on devnet with no upgrade authority
a whole bounty has been paid on the first deployment

of the pull requests #32, #33 and #34 by jaystay-bot, the ones that were merged and paid on devnet when the release ran. Measured: Knos #32, #33 and #34 by jaystay-bot, merged 2026-10-03 14:53 UTC and paid by the first deployment's knos_pay after its one-hour hold: knos due jaystay-bot read 'Paid for 3 pull request(s) in 1 repository: 48.75 in all' at 15:56 UTC; the payments are the knos:paid lines of issues #29, #30 and #31 in knos_pay's log on devnet
the fee the program takes at release: 0.30% of the amount, at least 0.05, paid by the funder on top (knos_pay FEE_BPS and FEE_MIN)

the fee the program takes at release, one rate and a floor, worked by hand in tests/data/billing_vectors.json and by tests/web/price.mjs: 1,000 pays 3.00; 5,000 pays 15.00; 100,000, the most an order holds on devnet, pays 300.00

Form 1099-NEC is filed for each person paid at least 2,000 USD in the course of business during the year, for tax years beginning after 2025 (IRS instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC, the IRS's own edition label (12/2026), read 10 Oct 2026)
cheating pull requests in the tamper benchmark (21 ideas in each of three sample repositories), and how many passed plain CI

what the program takes at release, shown before funding: fee = max(0.05, floor(amount x 30 / 10,000)); 5 pays 0.05 (1.00%), 20 pays 0.06, 100 pays 0.30, 1,000 pays 3, 5,000 pays 15, 100,000 pays 300 (0.30% each); a release under 16.67 pays the floor. The relayer's tip comes out of the fee

the fee on chain follows the build that is live: knos_pay 2.2 charges 0.30% with a minimum of 0.05; knos_pay 2.1, the public program until the upgrade to 2.2 executed on 9 Oct 2026, charged the 0.3.14 fee with a minimum of 0.40, and orders funded under it keep that fee (src/knos/fees.py NEW and OLD)

days of the time lock of the upgrade multisig: 691,200 seconds (192 hours), set by proposal 9, one action SetTimeLock { new_time_lock: 691200 } (docs/reference/GOVERNANCE.md). It executed on 11 Oct 2026, so the lock in force is 8 days; it was 48 hours before
the amounts of the fee's worked examples: 1,000 pays 3.00 and 5,000 pays 15.00, both 0.30% (tests/data/billing_vectors.json, on_chain.fees)
